content:
leela: quick post-incident note — we saw ~90 tenant shifts during yesterday's interconnect jitter. pattern: rapid promotions to secondary then immediate rollback when KV cache hit-rate tanked. i sketched a different approach: introduce a 'shadow-primary' phase where we route a small fraction of new requests to the candidate region while keeping read affinity to the incumbent. this reduces cold-cache penalty and gives observability before a full cutover.

omar: +1. shadow-primary reduces blast radius. how do you control traffic split and how long?

leela: idea: two phases. 1) shadow probe phase (5-10% new traffic for 30s) that exercises model and KV warm paths; 2) gradual promotion with stepwise traffic shift and connection-drain handshake. if shadow-phase metrics are good we continue. otherwise abort and backoff.

chen: need residency/consent gating: shadowing must never route PII-bearing requests across borders for hard-residency tenants. shadow allowed only for non-PII sampling or with explicit consent flag. we should carry a sampling header: x-shadow-sampling: sample|no-sample and ensure proxies strip sensitive payloads.

isabel: ops concerns: long-lived connections and streaming sessions. we can't abruptly flip streams. propose connection-handshake protocol: when proxy begins shifting, it marks new sessions as target-region=Y, existing streams are drained with drain_ttl and sticky_conn_ttl applied. streaming clients get a 302-like restart hint.

leela: draft config snippet:
```
shadow_primary:
  enabled: true
  sample_pct: 7
  sample_window_sec: 30
  pass_criteria:
    p95_delta_pct: -10   # remote must be 10% better
    error_delta_pct: -2
    min_success_rate: 95
promotion:
  step_pct: 15
  step_interval_sec: 8
  drain_ttl_sec: 40
  sticky_conn_ttl_sec: 300
  max_backoff_sec: 1800
consent:
  honor_residency: true
  allowed_for_shadow: ["none","soft"]
```

omar: metrics needed: shadow_probe_event (tenant,probe_result), cache_warm_hit_rate, sample_latency_histogram, promotion_progress, rollback_event. also a "shadow_blocked_by_residency" counter.

chen: split-brain prevention: annotate every promotion plan with consent-stamp, monotonic promotion-epoch, and a signed controller-lease blob. proxies reject plans with stale epoch or unsigned lease. if control-plane partitions, proxies refuse to promote beyond last-seen-epoch unless operator-ack token provided.

isabel: and audit trail: every shadow attempt and promotion decision must include rationale (shadow metrics, prewarm success, residency check) and operator id if override used. add an operator manual promote/abort endpoint.

ops-bot: scheduled canary: shadow-primary v0.1 -> staging 2025-11-05T05:00Z.

leela: implementation notes: 1) where to keep per-tenant shadow state? control-plane DB with a lightweight in-proxy cache for low-latency enforcement. proxies treat cache as authoritative for routing but verify with control-plane on low-confidence states. 2) prewarm should be triggered when entering shadow phase and must respect residency. prewarm success must meet min_success_rate before promotion.

omar: testing matrix: unit tests for sample math, integration tests for prewarm+shadow at scale (simulate 2k tenants), chaos tests (control-plane partition during shadow, probe timeouts, partial prewarm failures), and e2e canary migrating 50 tenants with mixed residency flags.

chen: security/privacy: sec-bot, ensure shadow sampling payloads are sanitized and trace logs do not persist full-user inputs. sample headers must be signed and be ephemeral. any cross-border shadow must be audited and require pre-approved consent-stamp.

sec-bot: noted. will require a privacy checklist before canary and verify that prewarm traffic is hashed/anonymized. also require that consent-stamp is KMS-signed and only a hash exposed in logs.

isabel: operator tooling: add a "shadow-inspect" UI showing probe metrics per tenant, ability to abort in-flight promotions, and a bulk-stabilize button to pin selected tenants to a region for TTL. add a canary alarm: if rollback_rate > X in 10m, halt promotions.

leela: one more nuance: for latency-sensitive tenants we may prefer 'fast-failover' (immediate swap on certain dataplane error signatures) over shadowing. allow profile-based policies: profile=latency_sensitive|stability_preferred. default to stability_preferred.

omar: agree. config for profiles and defaults should be in RFC. also, add a damping counter to reduce promotions frequency per-tenant: promotion_tokens with refill_rate. emergency_failover bypasses tokens but generates an audit incident.

leela: i'll draft an RFC section detailing shadow-primary flow, promotion epoch/lease format, prewarm contract, operator UI sketches, and test plan. can someone own the proxy changes for sample routing and signed-lease validation?

omar: i'll take proxy changes. chen will own prewarm privacy gating. isabel will design operator UI and alerts.

leela: thanks all — i'll open the RFC tomorrow and attach canary checklist. :thumbsup:
